\subsection{Programmable feedback resistor}\label{ss:tiarprog}

\texttt{anatop\_tia\_rprog} is the transimpedance gain element of the rev-2 channel:
a digitally programmable resistor that sets \(R_F\) between the TIA output and the
working-electrode virtual ground. Its law is
\[
R = 18\,\mathrm{k}\Omega + 6\,\mathrm{k}\Omega\cdot N,\qquad
N = \mathrm{bin}(\texttt{ResEn<5:0>}) + 64\cdot\mathrm{popcount}(\texttt{ThEn<3:0>}),
\]
\(N = 0\ldots 319\), so every \SI{6}{\kilo\ohm} value from \SI{18}{\kilo\ohm} to
\SI{1.932}{\mega\ohm} is reachable and the map is monotonic by construction. The
ladder is a series chain of identical poly units --- a three-unit fixed base, six
binary-weighted segments of 1 to 32 units, and four thermometer segments of 64
units --- each switched segment shunted by a CMOS bypass transmission gate
(the thermometer gates at twice the binary gates' width;
Figure~\ref{fig:tiarprog-switch}). A control bit at 1
opens its gate and inserts the segment; terminals are \texttt{A}, \texttt{B} and
the ten control bits, with the gate supplies arriving by inherited connection.

The endpoints follow from the converter, not from the ladder. The SAR's effective
input window is \SI{1.63}{\volt}, \(\pm\SI{0.815}{\volt}\) about
\(V_{\mathrm{CM}}\) (\S\ref{ss:adc}), essentially coincident with the TIA's
measured \(\pm\SI{0.80}{\volt}\) compliance. At \(N=0\)
(\SI{19.6}{\kilo\ohm} typical) that window carries \(\pm\SI{40.7}{\micro\ampere}\),
covering the \(\pm\SI{33}{\micro\ampere}\) application target; at \(N=319\)
(\SI{1.931}{\mega\ohm}) the range is \(\pm\SI{0.41}{\micro\ampere}\) with a
current quantum of \SI{0.82}{\nano\ampere}, an order above the
\SI{49}{\pico\ampere} the loop actually delivers in the amperometric band
(Section~\ref{sss:tiarprog-noise}), so at maximum gain the resolution floor is
quantisation rather than noise. Larger \(R_F\) would buy nothing: the noise
floor does not shrink with \(R_F\), and headroom does --- at
\(V_{\mathrm{CM}}=\SI{1.25}{\volt}\) on \SI{2.5}{\volt} the top code can carry at
most \(\approx\SI{0.65}{\micro\ampere}\) before the terminal voltage rails.

All data is schematic-level; the cell has no layout view yet. The bench forces
\SI{500}{\nano\ampere} through \texttt{A}--\texttt{B} with \texttt{B} held at
\(V_{\mathrm{CM}}\) and reads \(R\) from the terminal voltage; one swept variable
decodes into all ten control bits, and the decode was verified against an
independent per-code deck to \SI{0.18}{\ohm} over all 320 codes.
